introduction: ERC-2009 defines a Compliance Service interface that lets regulated tokens run KYC and AML checks fully on-chain before a transfer, mint, or burn executes. It was proposed by Daniel Lehrner in May 2019. Tokens query check functions that return a status code of 0x11 (Allowed) or 0x10 (Disallowed), then record limits through update functions in the same transaction. Note: ERC-2009 is Stagnant — it has been inactive for 6+ months and may never be finalized, but remains historically or technically significant.
designPurpose: ERC-2009 was designed to decentralize compliance checks for regulated tokens. Before it, KYC and AML verification often ran off-chain, which centralized transfers and forced a slower, non-atomic second confirmation step. ERC-1462 proposed which checks a token needs but not how to implement them. ERC-2009 answers this with an on-chain interface of check and update functions, leaving the rule logic to implementers, and keys state to a bytes32 token id so a token can upgrade its contract without migrating its data.
commonUsage: The Compliance Service is intended for regulated and security tokens that must enforce KYC, AML, and jurisdiction-specific transfer limits directly in the contract. Because one service can register many tokens by bytes32 id, it is designed so a law-maker or issuer can maintain shared compliance rules for every token in a jurisdiction. As a Stagnant proposal it never saw broad production adoption; on-chain compliance in practice is more commonly handled by permissioned-token frameworks such as ERC-3643.
fn.checkTransferAllowed.desc: Checks whether a transfer of the given value from one holder to another is permitted for the token, returning a status code; the token must revert unless the code is 0x11 (Allowed).
fn.checkTransferAllowed.params.tokenId: The unique bytes32 ID that identifies the token.
fn.checkTransferAllowed.params.from: The payer address the tokens would be taken from if executed.
fn.checkTransferAllowed.params.to: The payee address the tokens would be transferred to if executed.
fn.checkTransferAllowed.params.value: The amount that would be transferred.
fn.checkTransferAllowed.returns.status: A status code, 0x11 (Allowed) or 0x10 (Disallowed), or an issuer-specific equivalent.
fn.checkMintAllowed.desc: Checks whether minting the given value to a payee is permitted for the token, returning a status code that the token must treat as a precondition of the mint.
fn.checkMintAllowed.params.tokenId: The unique bytes32 ID that identifies the token.
fn.checkMintAllowed.params.to: The payee address that would receive the minted tokens.
fn.checkMintAllowed.params.value: The amount that would be minted.
fn.checkMintAllowed.returns.status: A status code, 0x11 (Allowed) or 0x10 (Disallowed), or an issuer-specific equivalent.
fn.checkBurnAllowed.desc: Checks whether burning the given value from a holder is permitted for the token, returning a status code that must be 0x11 (Allowed) for the burn to proceed.
fn.checkBurnAllowed.params.tokenId: The unique bytes32 ID that identifies the token.
fn.checkBurnAllowed.params.from: The payer address the tokens would be burned from.
fn.checkBurnAllowed.params.value: The amount that would be burned.
fn.checkBurnAllowed.returns.status: A status code, 0x11 (Allowed) or 0x10 (Disallowed), or an issuer-specific equivalent.
fn.updateTransferAccumulated.desc: Records the accumulated totals for a transfer and must be called in the same transaction as the transfer; it reverts if the update violates any compliance rule. The rule logic is left to the implementer.
fn.updateTransferAccumulated.params.toke: The unique bytes32 ID that identifies the token.
fn.updateTransferAccumulated.params.from: The payer address the tokens are taken from.
fn.updateTransferAccumulated.params.to: The payee address the tokens are transferred to.
fn.addToken.desc: Registers a token with the service under a bytes32 ID so it may call the update functions; it reverts if the ID is already in use. Whether registration is restricted is left to the implementer. Emits TokenAdded.
fn.addToken.params.tokenId: The unique bytes32 ID to assign to the token.
fn.addToken.params.token: The address from which the update functions will be called.
fn.authorizeAccumulatedOperator.desc: Approves an operator to update the accumulated totals on behalf of the caller's token id. Returns true on success and emits AuthorizedAccumulatedOperator.
fn.authorizeAccumulatedOperator.params.o: The address to approve as an operator of accumulated updates.
True if the operator was approved.
fn.revokeAccumulatedOperator.desc: Revokes an operator's approval to update the accumulated totals on behalf of the caller's token id. Returns true on success and emits RevokedAccumulatedOperator.
fn.revokeAccumulatedOperator.params.oper: The address to revoke as an operator of accumulated updates.
fn.revokeAccumulatedOperator.returns.suc: True if the operator's approval was revoked.
fn.TokenAdded.desc: Emitted after a token has been added to the service.
fn.TokenAdded.params.tokenId: The unique bytes32 ID that identifies the token.
fn.TokenAdded.params.token: The address from which the update functions will be called.
fn.AuthorizedAccumulatedOperator.desc: Emitted when an operator is approved to update the accumulated on behalf of a token.
The address approved as an operator of accumulated updates.
The token id on whose behalf accumulated updates may be made.
fn.RevokedAccumulatedOperator.desc: Emitted when an operator is revoked from updating the accumulated on behalf of a token.
fn.RevokedAccumulatedOperator.params.ope: The address whose operator approval was revoked.
fn.RevokedAccumulatedOperator.params.tok: The token id on whose behalf accumulated updates could be made.
sim.complianceCheckWalkthrough.name: Compliance Check Walkthrough
sim.complianceCheckWalkthrough.desc: Follow a regulated token as it registers with the service, checks a transfer, and records the accumulated total.
sim.complianceCheckWalkthrough.step.regi: The token is registered with the service by addToken, which stores its address under a bytes32 id and emits TokenAdded.
sim.complianceCheckWalkthrough.step.chec: Before the transfer, the token calls checkTransferAllowed and the service returns 0x11 (Allowed).
sim.complianceCheckWalkthrough.step.upda: In the same transaction, the token calls updateTransferAccumulated, which updates the accumulated total or reverts on a rule breach.
